successors.name: Qi (state)
successors.text: Lai, 'located in what is now eastern Shandong Province' on 'the tip of the Shandong Peninsula bordering Qi' (Changle, Linqu, Ni; place names Laiwu, Laixi, Laizhou, Laiyang)

ledger.x: c. 1046: Lai is already beside the new Qi. The page gives no founding ('Established: ?') and says only that 'As soon as Jiang Ziya, the first ruler of Qi, was enfeoffed at Qi, the state of Lai attacked its capital at Yingqiu'; the Zhou-conquest year is a bridge.
567: Duke Ling of Qi crushes Lai.
567: the state of Lai ends in Qi's conquest; 'The people (Dongyi) were moved to Laiwu.'

wars.name: Qi conquest of Lai
wars.outcome: Lai attacked Qi in 567 BC, was decisively defeated by Duke Ling of Qi and its duke killed; Qi annexed the state and moved its people to Laiwu.

certainty.note: No Lai boundary is on the page; soft throughout.
